# Production chat rendering assets

`npm ci && npm run vendor:chat-renderer` rebuilds the new assets from exact package pins. Existing rich-transcript.js and its older renderer recipe remain unchanged. The older PROVENANCE.md MathML-only note describes that legacy renderer; production typed chat uses KaTeX HTML plus accessible MathML and its complete local CSS/fonts.

- Mermaid 11.17.2 stays within the native artifact's declared ^11.16.0 range. The native exact lock resolution was not supplied, so bit-identical renderer layout is not asserted. 11.17.2 removes known 11.16.0 CSS/prototype/DoS advisories.
- Mermaid's nested KaTeX is overridden to the existing exact safe KaTeX 0.19.0. npm ls katex confirms a deduplicated dependency, rather than the older nested 0.16.47. This changes nested math implementation relative to that unresolved native lock.
- Shiki 4.5.0 uses its JavaScript regex engine, without evaluation or WebAssembly. Local bundled languages: JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON, CSS, HTML, Python, Bash, Markdown, SQL, Diff. Unknown languages and failed imports retain plain code.
- marked-footnote 1.4.0 provides GFM footnote parsing and rendering. Its npm package omits the license file; the checked-in MIT license comes from its exact published gitHead faab750f00af4788397948286fb8f7fe0c929a7e. The build validates that license SHA-256. Other bundled dependency licenses are copied from installed packages; fastdom's full MIT text is copied from its README.
- KaTeX 0.19.0 CSS is byte-identical upstream CSS, including its one global equation counter reset. All 60 local font files are preserved. Application prose styles are scoped to typed conversation content and its owned diagram dialog.

The JSON manifest records generated assets and bundled package version/licenses. Rebuilding cleans old Mermaid/Shiki chunks. Registry integrity remains in package-lock.json.

Ordinary Markdown escapes raw HTML and prevents Markdown image fetching. Only HTTP(S) links receive external navigation. Generated math has separate sanitation and a finite style grammar. Footnote IDs originate in parsed extension output, are prefixed per conversation/message, and validated after sanitation. Footnote navigation targets exact IDs inside that same entry only. The visible Footnotes heading follows the fresh user-provided native screenshot rather than mdast's generic hidden-heading default. User HTML cannot create IDs or executable controls. Checklist inputs are created from parsed task tokens and disabled.

Mermaid uses strict security, HTML labels disabled, base theme and current transcript colors. Never call bindFunctions. Generated SVG receives a separate tag/attribute/style allowlist, scoped IDs and local-fragment-only references. Unsafe diagrams retain readable source plus error. Own conservative limits: 20000 code units, 500 edges; reject configuration directives, YAML frontmatter (including config overrides), click directives, embedded images and network/file/data URLs before rendering. Inline SVG label constructs requiring foreignObject fail to readable source instead of dropping labels. Typed content and the body-appended viewer use scoped active light/dark transcript aliases with native S36-S39 neutral semantics; Mermaid and PNG backgrounds use the active elevated fill, independent of the injected light Sand defaults and unrelated Cursor palette. Async imports/render/highlighting/clipboard/export carry owner/revision/generation/disposal checks. Retained nested blocks advance their current owner on every accepted context update, including unchanged parent spans. One dialog per surface, source fit/clamp/pan/wheel/zoom constants and real PNG pixels. Export uses actual sanitized SVG, current elevated fill, scale 2 bounded at 8192 pixels, 5000ms decode timeout, 3000ms warning and mermaid-diagram.png.

Projector verification: 57 source-contract Node cases passed. Browser interaction, geometry/pixels, theme and retention acceptance belong to the root's actual application e2e run; this note does not claim those gates passed.
